ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: a hunting season
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Six days of hunting. Each morning two of the land's wild animals are marked for the colony's hunters: those with the most meat that are safe to hunt. A tribe calls it the hunters' moon, a village opens the hunting season, an industrial colony takes out a game licence and a spacer colony calls it a cull; the hunting is the same. The hunters spend more time hunting and less at other work, and a hunted animal may still fight back, as in any hunt. Nothing is marked while nobody is set to hunt and has a weapon fit for it. The bloodthirsty love it and hunters and gourmands like it; the kind dislike it, and those whose ideoligion holds hunting or violence wrong hate it.

effects.li: Each morning for six days, two wild animals are marked for the hunters: those with the most meat that are safe to hunt, never a predator, an insect, anything very large or anything likely to fight back.
The colony's hunters go after them as they would any animal marked for hunting, and a hunted animal may still fight back.
The bloodthirsty love it and hunters and gourmands like it; the kind dislike it, and those whose ideoligion holds hunting or violence wrong hate it.

plain.li: The cold is coming and the meat store is half empty, so let the hunters go out every day.
[tribal] It's the hunters' moon, and every camp of my people would be out after the herds by now.
[medieval] Open the season, and we'll have salt meat in the cellar by the first frost.
[industrial] A week of hunting, and the smokehouse full before the snow.
[spacer] A short cull while the herds are fat would keep the freezer full through the winter.

blunt.li: There's meat walking about out there and we're eating oats.

cheerful.li: Out at first light every morning, I can't wait.

cold.li: Game is food we don't have to grow.

plain.li: Two a day for six days is a lot of the land's animals.
I'd rather the hunters went out when we need meat, not every morning by rule.

warm.li: The herds come back to that meadow every year, and I like seeing them there.

gloomy.li: Somebody will get gored, and then we'll stop.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: wood for the winter
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Eight days of felling. Each morning up to six of the nearest wild trees outside the home area are marked for cutting, until the stores hold enough wood for the winter: 150 per colonist for a tribe or a village, which burns wood in every hearth, and 80 for an industrial or spacer colony, which needs it for its workbenches and generators. The cutters spend their time felling and the haulers bring the wood in. The industrious, hard workers and the tough like it; the lazy dislike it, and those whose ideoligion holds tree cutting wrong hate it.

effects.li: Each morning for eight days, up to six of the nearest wild trees outside the home area are marked for cutting, until the stores hold the winter's wood: 150 per colonist for a tribe or a village, 80 for any other colony.
The colony's cutters fell them as they would any tree marked for cutting, and the haulers bring in the wood.
The industrious, hard workers and the tough like it; the lazy dislike it, and those whose ideoligion holds tree cutting wrong hate it.

plain.li: The woodpile won't see us to spring, so let's fill it while the ground is dry.
[lowtech] Every hearth burns wood all winter, and we'd better have it cut before the snow.
[!lowtech] The benches and the generators eat timber, and the forest is right there.

blunt.li: Cold people don't work, so cut the wood.

cheerful.li: Nothing like an axe in autumn to warm you up.

cold.li: Wood now costs a week; wood in midwinter costs fingers.

plain.li: Eight days of nothing but trees, and the rest of the work piling up behind them.

warm.li: That stand of trees by the stream is the prettiest thing on the land.

gloomy.li: We'll cut it all and still be cold.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: foraging days
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Six days of gathering wild food. Each morning up to twelve ripe wild plants near the colony that give food (berries, agave, mushrooms) are marked for harvesting, the nearest first. A tribe calls them berry days, a village gleans the hedges, and an industrial or spacer colony surveys what the land grows; the picking is the same. The growers spend more time on wild plants and less in the fields. Those with a passion for growing and ascetics like it; undergrounders and the industrious dislike it.

effects.li: Each morning for six days, up to twelve ripe wild plants within 45 cells of the middle of the colony and outside its growing zones are marked for harvesting, the nearest first: only plants that give food, never medicine, a drug or a tree.
The colony's growers pick them as they would any plant marked for harvesting, which takes time from the fields.
Those with a passion for growing and ascetics like it; undergrounders and the industrious dislike it.

plain.li: The bushes along the stream are heavy with berries and nobody's picking them.
[lowtech] My grandmother knew every bush within a day's walk, and so should we.
[!lowtech] Free food growing a short walk from the gate, and we buy ours from traders.

warm.li: A basket of berries every morning would make the whole colony smile.

cold.li: It's food that costs nothing but a walk.

plain.li: Picking berries when the field needs weeding.

gloomy.li: Half of it will be eaten by the birds before we get there.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: saving the power
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Five nights of saving the power. Every lamp of the colony's is switched off at eleven at night and on again at five in the morning, except in a room where a patient is in a medical bed. The power the lamps would have used stays in the batteries, and anyone up at night works in the dark. Only for a colony that has researched electricity; a tribe or a village banks its fires instead. Those whose ideoligion prefers darkness love it, and ascetics and undergrounders like it; night owls hate it, and the nervous and the volatile dislike it.

effects.li: Every lamp of the colony's is switched off from eleven at night to five in the morning (never one in a room with a patient in a medical bed), and switched on again after.
The power the lamps would have used stays in the batteries.
Those whose ideoligion prefers darkness love it, and ascetics and undergrounders like it; night owls hate it, and the nervous and the volatile dislike it.

plain.li: The batteries are flat by dawn, and the lamps burn all night in empty rooms.
[industrial] Lights out at eleven, the way it was in the mill towns.
[spacer] Dim the habitat at night and the cells will last.

blunt.li: Nobody needs a lamp to sleep.

cold.li: Every lamp lit at three in the morning is power we'll want at noon.

plain.li: I do my best work at night, and now I'll do it in the dark.

gloomy.li: Something will come at the walls the one night it's dark.

cheerful.li: Fine, but I'm keeping a candle under my bed.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: every faith its evening
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: For ten days the council treats every ideoligion in the colony alike. When it is declared, the largest ideoligion that isn't the colony's own holds an evening of faith, if one can be held. Each morning those of other ideoligions trust the council a little more (a quarter to half a point, more for the open-minded), and the devout of the colony's own ideoligion trust it a quarter point less. It can't be declared while one ideoligion is named the colony's, and that decree can't be declared while this one holds. Only with Ideology and more than one ideoligion at home. Those of other ideoligions love it, and the kind and those whose ideoligion frowns on being preached to like it; the devout of the colony's own dislike it.

effects.li: When it is declared, the largest ideoligion at home that isn't the colony's own holds an evening of faith, if one can be held.
Each morning those of other ideoligions trust the council a little more (a quarter to half a point, the open-minded most); the devout of the colony's own ideoligion trust it a quarter point less.
Those of other ideoligions love it and the kind like it; the devout of the colony's own dislike it. Never together with one ideoligion for the colony.

plain.li: Half of us pray to something else, and the council should say that's welcome here.
[newcomer] The new ones don't share our ideoligion, and they should know they don't have to.

warm.li: Let every ideoligion here have its evening, and let's all be the better for it.

cold.li: People who feel welcome don't make trouble.

plain.li: The colony has an ideoligion, and the council should stand by it.

gloomy.li: Every faith its evening, and soon nobody keeps any of them.
